title: Expose catalog pagination in the public OpenAPI contract
prompt:
Document the existing catalog pagination contract for generated clients. Evidence: src/app/api/openapi.json/route.ts:166-175 describes the catalog as listing all tools, declares no query parameters, and exposes only tools and total in its response schema. Local execution of GET confirmed that limit, offset, and the 400 response are absent. The catalog already defaults to 50 rows, caps its effective limit at 100, accepts category and offset, and returns the effective limit and offset. Clients generated from this public spec cannot discover how to request the remaining tools.

Change only src/app/api/openapi.json/route.ts in production. Add optional limit, offset, and category query parameters to the catalog operation. Document digit-only positive safe-integer limits, default 50, and clamping above 100; do not claim values above 100 are rejected. Document nonnegative safe-integer offset with default zero and overflow rejection. Include returned limit and offset properties, clarify that total counts the returned page, and describe the existing 400 validation response. Preserve all unrelated operations and security definitions. Do not alter catalog behavior or filtering policy.

Add exactly one new test file, tests/openapi-catalog-pagination.test.ts. Execute the real OpenAPI GET with in-memory TypeScript transpilation and a NextResponse stub. Assert parameter names, locations, optionality, defaults, accurate clamping wording, response properties, page-local total description, and 400 response. Run node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/openapi-catalog-pagination.test.ts. No credentials, deploys, sends, payments, migrations, workflows, package.json, or auth changes. Do not commit or push; work on the assigned branch you are on.
